title: Love’s in Sight!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Morio Kurokawa, an intimidating 18-year-old dropout and former delinquent known for winning fights, falls for Yukiko Akaza, a 16-year-old student at a school for the blind who has very limited sight. As they grow closer, Yukiko's protective older sister Izumi is unsure about him, and everyday outings bring up questions of accessibility and respect. A romantic comedy told in short chapters.
life_message: Everyone deserves to be treated with respect, and love grows when people see each other as whole persons rather than labels.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Equal treatment of blind and sighted people is the message.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Personal dignity and tolerance over security.

folkways.japan: The reformed yankee (delinquent) with a soft heart is a familiar Japanese archetype, and tactile paving and audio guides reflect Japan's public accessibility features.

delivery.evidence: ANN: 'very solid messaging' on respect; adaptive details appear 'without it feeling like a learning experience'; Izumi's storyline heavy-handed.
delivery.note: Ableist attitudes appear in minor figures who are corrected, and the overprotective sister is shown with signs of caregiver burnout rather than as a villain.

winners_losers: Morio and Yukiko's mutual respect wins; dismissive or overprotective attitudes are shown as obstacles to grow past.
